try-the-manual-controls.text: The simulator has two explicit profiles. The first-release naming profile lets you queue competing claims for alice, fold the winner, observe the duplicate refusal, resolve the certified fixture, and try a refused Delete. The generic registry profile separately demonstrates Insert withdrawal, address evolution, retirement, Delete, and batch ordering. Neither profile silently falls back to the other.

Naming payment-destination maintenance, committed-controller recovery, and controller-or-quorum retirement are specified but not called playable before their integrated transitions and browser assertions land. Naming withdrawal remains on hold and has no control. In the generic profile, queue two Inserts, fold one, separately approve and withdraw the other, then explore evolution and terminal requests.

what-the-evidence-establishes.text: This simulator candidate replays fifty-eight generic Lean rows and thirty-four naming rows. Forty-one generic declarations and seventeen naming declarations are proved from the standard axioms. The generic ledger has twelve controlled checks, seventeen exhibits only, and twelve gaps; naming has fifteen controlled checks, two exhibits only, and no gaps. The gate also exercises one thousand seven hundred and seventy-two public-boundary probes and forty-three negative controls. These are finite checks, not acceptance.

model-and-assumptions.text: The generic model uses tagged commitments and logical lists for maps and UTxOs. Application acceptance and witnesses are supplied evidence; scripts and signatures are not verified here. Generic refund values are commitments rather than modeled payments. The current playable naming card still uses finite predecessor fixtures. The lifecycle contract requires an explicit controller-address shape and thirty-two-byte next-controller commitment, which are not called playable before engine and browser integration.

reproduce-the-focused-checks.text: Use the simulator build check, Node gate, and gate self-test from the repository root. The standalone page embeds both profile engines and its runtime assets. The pinned browser check exercises generic and naming controls, refusal branches, both themes, and a mobile viewport. Build the documentation release for a reproducible review bundle with raw model, contract, scenarios, replay sources, pinned tooling, exact identities, and SHA two hundred and fifty six manifests. It remains review material, not a published release or ledger artifact.
